messages:
Maya Patel: Taking over as primary for the night shift — quick summary up front. Two active alerts: INC-42879 (KV cache evictions causing increased tail latency) and INC-42880 (embeddings-queue backlog). Im on-call until 02:00 UTC, Ahmed is secondary, Sara is warm on-call.

Maya Patel: Customer impact: some Hosted API customers and a subset of Dedicated tenants in us-west are seeing 5-15% increased p99 latency and sporadic 429s for short bursts. No full outages. See dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/42879 (kv) and https://console.redwood/alerts/42880 (embeddings).

PagerDuty: Incident INC-42879 acknowledged by Ahmed Khan at 1788888905.

Ahmed Khan: ack. digging into eviction metrics now. first impression: cold-start evictions correlated with recent config rollout to kv-cache pool that tightened memory limits.

Maya Patel: Mitigations in progress:
- Autoscaling bumped for embeddings workers (+2 replicas) to drain backlog (OpsBot triggered).
- Temporarily increased kv-cache memory cap on pool-4 to prevent further evictions.
- Disabled prefetching for lower-priority tenants to reduce churn.
- Rolling rollback queued for the config change that looks suspicious; holding until we confirm.

OpsBot: autoscaler: embeddings-queue scaled from 6 -> 8 replicas (reason: queue_depth > 80%). Timestamp: 1788888920.

Ahmed Khan: Running quick checks. Commands I ran:
```
# check eviction events
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=kv-cache | grep eviction | tail -n 50
# inspect mem pressure on nodes
kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -r | head
```
Found spikes on node gpu-usw2-05 correlated with eviction bursts.

InfraRunbookBot: Runbook KV-EVICTION (internal): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction. Key steps: increase pool memory, toggle eviction-safety flag, consider short-lived cache warmers.

Sara Liu: Heads-up: EU region has no secondary between 00:30-03:00 UTC (coverage gap). If the issue spreads to eu-west we'll be light. I can extend if needed but would prefer Ahmed to handle handoff after 02:00 UTC.

Liam O'Connor: Noted customer impact from the support queue: ~12 tickets mentioning slow responses, a couple referencing "generation timeout". Most on Dedicated customers with pinned model variants. Recommend running targeted fallback to smaller q4 model for affected tenants if latency keeps rising.

Maya Patel: Planned short-term actions (next 30m):
- Keep embeddings scaled and watch queue drain (ops).
- Monitor evictions after memory bump; if they drop to baseline, rollback will be canceled.
- If evictions persist > 10m, proceed with rollback of config change.
- If p99 > 1.5s for more than 15m for >3 tenants, initiate targeted fallback routing.

Ahmed Khan: Im doing an incremental rollback of the kv-cache memory-limits change on canary nodes now. Patch command:
```
kubectl -n inference patch deploy kv-cache-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kv-cache","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"6Gi"}}}]}}}}'
```
Applying to 2 canaries first.

Maya Patel: If rollback doesn't reduce evictions in 10m, we should consider temporary config: `eviction-safety: strict -> warning` (see runbook). That will reduce evictions but increases memory usage.

PagerDuty: Incident INC-42880 (embeddings backlog) automatically created at 1788888945.

Ahmed Khan: embeddings backlog is dropping after scaling, current queue_depth: 42 (was 180). Continuing watch.

OpsBot: alert manager silenced for non-critical prefetch alerts (30m).

Liam O'Connor: Quick note on customer impact classification: set incident severity to S2 for now. Were seeing latency but not full outage, and CAPEX customers on Dedicated are affected. Will escalate to S1 if error rates > 3% or sustained >30min.

Sara Liu: I can jump in to handle eu-west if it looks like spillover — will keep pager reachable. For now, main action is rollback and monitor.

Maya Patel: Handing off current state to Ahmed at 02:00 UTC unless issue worsens. My contact: maya@redwood.com, Slack DM and phone. Leaving checklist for Ahmed:
- Verify eviction metric (evictions/min) after rollback.
- Keep embeddings scaling until queue < 20 and stable for 10m.
- Watch for new deploys (put a soft block on kv-cache deploys for 90m).
- If any Dedicated tenant reports >5% errors escalate S1 and page on-call leads.

Ahmed Khan: Ill take over at 02:00 UTC. Im going to keep the rollback running on canaries and if green promote to pool-4. Will post updates here.

Maya Patel: One-off commands / diagnostics that helped earlier:
```
# eviction timeline
/opt/bin/eviction_tool --since 1788888600 --format=summary
# quick health check
curl -sS https://internal-health/redwood/kv/pool-4/metrics | jq '.evictions, .mem_used'
```

Liam O'Connor: FYI support is sending a templated update to affected customers: short explanation + ETA to stabilize (~30-45m). Approved.

Maya Patel: Leaving the thread now to run a quick runbook action. Will check back right before 02:00 UTC. If anything spikes, tag @Ahmed Khan directly. :wave:

Ahmed Khan: ack and thanks. Updating PagerDuty notes.

PagerDuty: INC-42879 notes updated by Ahmed Khan at 1788889300.

OpsBot: autoscaler: embeddings-queue scaling event complete; queue depth 18.

Ahmed Khan: Can confirm canary rollback reduced eviction spikes on canaries. Monitoring results for next 15m before promoting.

Maya Patel: (reaction :thumbsup:) great. good handoff.

Liam O'Connor: leaving this on watch. tagging support lead in case we need customer comms: @support-team.

Sara Liu: If you promote rollback to pool-4, remember to toggle monitor threshold back to normal after 30m to avoid noisy alerts.

Maya Patel: End of notes from me. Good luck team.

(End of thread)
